mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month, coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000, signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit from increased activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST increases for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a loosening monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market liquidity improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS increases for two consecutive months.
